categories.main_business_segments: Shenzhen Expressway Corporation Limited primarily operates in toll highway investment, construction, operation, and management, alongside general environmental protection businesses including solid waste recycling treatment and clean energy power generation. The company also provides construction management, highway operation management services, intelligent transportation, engineering management, and industrial financial services. It has diversified into upstream and downstream industry chain services such as operation and maintenance, engineering management, industry finance, and digital technology.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs advanced technologies such as Building Information Modelling (BIM) for construction management, electronic toll collection (ETC) systems for toll operations, and digital intelligence platforms for smart transportation. In environmental protection, it uses efficient anaerobic reaction treatment and MBR membrane bioreactors for organic waste treatment. The clean energy segment focuses on wind power and photovoltaic technologies, with integrated business capabilities in investment, operation, maintenance, and financing of renewable energy projects.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary customers include government entities and enterprises requiring toll highway services, environmental protection solutions, and clean energy power generation. The toll highway business serves urban and regional transportation needs, especially in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and other economically developed regions in China. Environmental services cater to municipal solid waste management and renewable energy markets, while financial services support infrastructure and industrial clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in Shenzhen and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, with additional projects in other provinces such as Hunan, Jiangsu, Guizhou, Inner Mongolia, and Xinjiang. Its toll highway projects cover approximately 613 kilometers of high-grade highways primarily in economically developed regions. The environmental and clean energy businesses have a nationwide presence, including wind power projects in northwest China and organic waste treatment facilities in multiple provinces.
categories.supply_chain_position: Shenzhen Expressway Corporation Limited operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the infrastructure supply chain. It invests in, constructs, operates, and manages toll highways and environmental protection facilities. The company also extends upstream into project development, engineering consulting, and construction management, and downstream into operation and maintenance services, digital technology applications, and industrial financial services, thereby covering a broad spectrum of the infrastructure value chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus includes consolidating and expanding its core toll highway business while developing the general environmental protection and clean energy sectors. It emphasizes digital transformation and smart transportation technologies to enhance operational efficiency and service quality. R&D efforts concentrate on BIM technology, intelligent transportation systems, green recycling technologies for waste and batteries, and innovation in renewable energy projects. The company is preparing its 15th Five-Year Development Strategy to align with national policies and industry trends for sustainable growth.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through toll collection on highways, fees from environmental protection services such as organic waste treatment and clean energy power generation, and construction service fees under concession arrangements. Additional income streams include investment income from associates and joint ventures, property development, financial leasing services, and digital technology services. The company also receives government subsidies and compensation related to toll adjustments and environmental projects.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Shenzhen Expressway Corporation Limited is a leading state-owned infrastructure platform in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, holding a significant scale of toll highway assets and environmental projects. It competes with other domestic expressway operators and environmental service providers, leveraging its geographic advantages, comprehensive integrated management capabilities, innovation capacity, and strong financing platform. The company maintains a leading market position in toll highway investment and operation among listed domestic expressway companies.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the Group reported revenue of approximately RMB9.25 billion with a slight year-on-year decrease of 0.53%. Net profit attributable to shareholders was RMB1.145 billion, down 50.80% mainly due to reduced real estate income and asset impairment provisions. The Group’s total assets stood at RMB67.56 billion with stable liabilities and equity. It operates 16 toll highway projects covering about 613 km and has significant investments in environmental protection and clean energy. The company maintains strong financing capabilities with diversified funding sources and a solid credit rating.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company emphasizes its role as a state-owned infrastructure platform with strategic geographic positioning in the Greater Bay Area, providing high-quality toll highway and environmental protection services. It differentiates through integrated management capabilities spanning investment, construction, operation, and maintenance, combined with innovative digital technologies and smart transportation solutions. Its diversified business model, including environmental protection and clean energy, supports sustainable development and long-term value creation. The company also focuses on stable shareholder returns and compliance with regulatory standards.
